retry_policy.name: Bounded k=2 retry policy (this engagement's standing rule, reused verbatim from Sprint 1-4)
retry_policy.rule: On a REJECTED verdict from a Review sub-task's checklist, exactly one retry of the failing sub-task is authorized, re-dispatched with the specific FAIL findings appended. A second REJECTED STOPS the story and escalates to the user.

retry_class_addendum.added: 2026-09-22, consensus-agent failure-mode/retry/rollback/escalation review finding 3 (DASH-STORY-027-REVIEW REJECTED remediation)
retry_class_addendum.problem: The single k=2 policy above implicitly treats every REJECTED verdict as engineering-remediable by Dev/QA re-dispatch. DASH-STORY-027-REVIEW's own AC-027-REVIEW-1 (no code/docstring/API response may assert crypto-shredding legally satisfies DPDP Act erasure -- OAQ-10 stays open) is a legal-sufficiency question. No amount of python-backend-engineer or integration-testing-engineer retrying changes whether OAQ-10 is settled; re-dispatching the same k=2 loop against a FAIL on AC-027-REVIEW-1 would be asking an engineer to fix a legal question by writing more code.

two_classes.definition: A FAIL traceable to a defect in the shipped code, tests, or docstrings that Dev/QA can actually change -- e.g. a missing disclosure, an untested path, an orchestrator leg reimplemented instead of extended.
two_classes.policy: Unchanged k=2: one retry of the failing Dev/QA sub-task, re-dispatched with the FAIL findings appended. UPDATED 2026-09-22 per SP5-DEC-101 (user decision, resolved) for DASH-STORY-027-REVIEW specifically: a second REJECTED on this class no longer STOPS the story -- it is logged as an escalated, disclosed follow-up risk instead, since DASH-STORY-027-REVIEW is now a non-blocking advisory gate. The base retry_policy.rule above ('a second REJECTED STOPS the story') still applies as the general default for any story with a genuinely BLOCKING review; it no longer applies to DASH-STORY-027-REVIEW's own engineering-remediable class, which this addendum overrides for that specific sub-task.
applies_to_dash_story_027_review: AC-027-REVIEW-2 (Zone 7 audit record contains no erased PII)
AC-027-REVIEW-4 (orchestrator's Zone 3/5/8 legs extended, not duplicated)

two_classes.definition: A FAIL traceable to a legal-sufficiency or regulatory-judgment question no engineering change can resolve -- specifically OAQ-10 (does crypto-shredding satisfy DPDP Act erasure) and any FAIL that turns on the same kind of unresolved legal question.
two_classes.policy: NO retry. Not re-dispatched to python-backend-engineer, integration-testing-engineer, or any implementer. Escalates directly and only to the user/a named legal-review step -- the same escalation_target this file's base retry_policy already names, but on the FIRST REJECTED, not after a wasted k=2 cycle.

retry_class_addendum.rule: A REJECTED verdict from DASH-STORY-027-REVIEW (or any future P1-gated review) must be triaged per-AC against these two classes before any retry is authorized. A single REJECTED verdict may contain FAILs from both classes -- the compliance/legal-judgment FAILs escalate immediately regardless of whether the engineering-remediable FAILs in the same verdict are retried.

retry_scope_addendum.rule: A REJECTED verdict against DASH-STORY-028-DEV (whether from DASH-STORY-028-QA's test run or DASH-STORY-028-REVIEW's gate) is retried SCOPED to the specific failing repository/service surface(s) -- one or more of Zone 2 (episodic), Zone 3 (semantic), Zone 5 (conflict-aware entity), Zone 7 (provenance), Zone 8-manifest (SqlManifestRepository/Zone8ConsolidationStore/Zone8SubjectKeyedArchiver/SubjectErasureCascadeService) -- named by AC-028-QA-3's or AC-028-REVIEW-3's per-surface check, not a full re-dispatch of all ~10 handlers/8 providers.
